title: Signal · Friday 30 October
overview: The ECB holds rates as energy pushes inflation to 3.8 percent, BBVA puts AI agents at the centre of a strong quarter, and Société Générale posts a record third quarter.
status_line: A short edition: only 3 of 49 fixed sources could be read (FINMA, finews.com, finews.ch); the rest failed with a WebFetch permission error (PROVENANCE_REQUIRED, permission request not answered), so most items come from searches.

top.headline: ECB holds rates as energy pushes euro area inflation to 3.8 percent
top.summary: The ECB's Governing Council kept its three key interest rates unchanged on 29 October, leaving the deposit facility rate at 2.50 percent, according to Eunews. Headline inflation rose to 3.8 percent in September from 3.2 percent in August, with energy inflation at 18.9 percent.
top.background: The ECB said underlying inflation has stayed broadly stable and wages show no material response so far, while financing conditions have tightened since its last meeting.
top.why: A hold with a rise openly discussed keeps euro deposit margins firm for European banks, but tighter financing conditions and weaker consumer confidence point to slower credit growth.
top.watch_next: The next monetary policy meeting is in December.

top.headline: BBVA lifts quarterly profit 19.1 percent and plans to industrialise AI agents
top.summary: BBVA reported third-quarter net attributable profit of about 3 billion euros, up 19.1 percent, and a nine-month return on tangible equity of 22 percent, according to its earnings call transcript. Management said a voice assistant resolves close to 90 percent of interactions in a pilot, and agents cut preparation time for some corporate risk work by up to 30 percent.
top.background: BBVA has been one of Europe's most outspoken banks on generative AI, and its chief executive described a framework to roll agents out across the bank.
top.why: It gives private and retail banks a concrete benchmark for agent results, measured in resolution rates and hours saved rather than pilots counted.

top.headline: Société Générale posts record quarter with net income up 24.1 percent
top.summary: Société Générale reported third-quarter group net income of 1,888 million euros, up 24.1 percent, on revenues of 7,173 million euros, up 7.8 percent. Operating expenses rose only 0.8 percent, taking the cost-to-income ratio to 57.1 percent from 61.0 percent, and return on tangible equity reached 13.0 percent.
top.background: The bank has been running a cost and simplification programme, and completed an extraordinary 1.5 billion euro buyback on 30 September. Its CET1 ratio stood at 13.4 percent.
top.why: Flat costs with rising revenue is the case European boards will want explained: whether it comes from discipline, technology or both shapes next year's budgets.

items.headline: Goldman Sachs expects AI to make family offices more sophisticated
items.summary: Darren Allaway, EMEA head of Goldman Sachs Apex, told finews that AI will fuel another wave of sophistication among family offices. He said their allocation to alternatives has not fallen and may have risen slightly, and that AI and the energy behind data centres are a leading investment theme.
items.why: Family offices served from Zurich and Geneva will expect their banks to match this level of tooling and research.

items.headline: LGT Capital Partners names Sascha Gruber chief executive from January 2027
items.summary: Sascha Gruber, at the firm since 2002, will succeed founder Roberto Paganoni as chief executive on 1 January 2027, subject to regulatory approval, according to finews. Paganoni moves to the group holding board. The Pfäffikon firm manages more than 120 billion dollars for over 750 institutional clients.
items.why: A first change at the top since 1998 for one of Switzerland's largest private markets houses, with strategy said to continue.

items.headline: Swiss wealth managers' alliance grows to 42 members and CHF 155 billion
items.summary: The Alliance of Swiss Wealth Managers admitted Targa 5 Advisors and GSK & Partners from 1 November, taking it to 42 members managing more than CHF 155 billion with over 1,710 staff, according to finews. In 2022 it represented CHF 103 billion.
items.why: Independent managers are scaling up collectively, which matters to custodian banks competing for their booking business.

items.headline: Swiss CFOs are at their most optimistic in a long time
items.summary: In Deloitte's autumn CFO survey, 61 percent of Swiss finance chiefs expect the economy to improve over the next 12 months and 8 percent expect it to worsen, according to finews. AI budgets average 0.9 percent of total spending.
items.why: Under one percent of spend on AI suggests most Swiss corporates are still early, a useful baseline for any AI budget discussion.
